## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design strict isolation in a shared GCP project when vendor components may be compromised, and to specify concrete controls across data paths and CI workflow.

## Key Concepts
- Tenant-scoped access controls for Storage and BigQuery
- IAM Conditions and per-tenant service accounts
- Data encryption with CMEK
- Network boundaries via PSC and VPC Service Controls
- Runtime monitoring and quick containment
- CI gate with synthetic tenants and rollback

## Code Example
```yaml
# example IAM Condition binding for a tenant
bindings:
- members:
  - serviceAccount:tenant-a-sa@proj.iam.gserviceaccount.com
  role: roles/bigquery.dataViewer
  condition:
    title: "Tenant isolation"
    expression: "resource.name.startsWith('projects/PROJECT/datasets/tenantA')"
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test drift between intended tenant boundaries and real access paths?
- What metrics and alerting would signal an attempted cross-tenant exfiltration?

## Why This Is Asked
This question tests practical, beginner-friendly security controls in a real GCP setup, ensuring policies translate to concrete implementation steps.

## Key Concepts
- Least-privilege IAM and per-endpoint service accounts
- API-layer tenant isolation with tenant_id controls and basic RLS
- Private networking (Private IP/PSC) for service-to-service communication
- CI/CD gate with rollback for misconfiguration prevention

## Code Example
```yaml
# Example CI check pseudo
- name: Scan IAM bindings
  run: gcloud projects get-iam-policy PROJECT_ID --format=yaml > policy.yaml
  
- name: Validate least privilege
  run: |
    # Check for overly broad roles
    if grep -q 'roles/owner\|roles/editor' policy.yaml; then
      echo "ERROR: Broad roles detected"
      exit 1
    fi
    # Verify service account usage
    echo "IAM policy validated"

- name: Rollback on failure
  run: gcloud projects set-iam-policy PROJECT_ID policy.yaml.bak
```
